question: Second-generation non-sedating antihistamines (e.g., cetirizine, loratadine) are preferred over first-generation antihistamines (e.g., chlorpheniramine) for allergic rhinitis because they do not cross the blood-brain barrier significantly and avoid sedation and impaired psychomotor function.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is true. Prescribing sedating first-generation antihistamines to students and working adults is one of the most common management errors in allergic rhinitis. Non-sedating second-generation antihistamines should be the routine choice.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. First-generation antihistamines (chlorpheniramine, promethazine) are lipophilic and cross the blood-brain barrier, causing sedation, impaired concentration, and psychomotor dysfunction — a significant hazard for students, drivers, and professionals. Second-generation agents are the standard of care.
